absent: Numeric values and widths for LOCKSTAT_POINTS, MAX_LOCKDEP_SUBCLASSES, MAX_LOCKDEP_KEYS, MUTEX_FLAGS and its WAITERS HANDOFF PICKUP bits, LOCK_USAGE_CHARS, debug fill patterns, and bounce and timing counter types.
Complete record definitions with field order, sizes, alignment, and padding for lock maps, held entries, classes, statistics, timing summaries, tasks, interrupt history, mutexes, and waiters.
Contents of the shared state catalogue and the concrete mapping from abstract states to usage bits, initial-use sentinels, name tables, and verbose handlers.

Behavior and guarantees of external helpers for tracing, clocks, hashing, RCU traversal, interrupt save and restore, processor identity, symbol lookup, list handling, warnings, dumps, console emergency sections, cleanup guards, barriers, and hung-task tracking.
Lifecycle for class creation, registration, key assignment, and teardown, including hash insertion, eviction, reuse of indices, and interaction with validation disable.
Exact human-readable rendering, log levels, and stability promises for contention warnings, irq history dumps, held-lock listings, and kernel identification.

Concurrency and configuration effects beyond the shown guards, such as scheduler interaction, migration, real-time preemption treatment of soft state, statistics overflow and wraparound, and multiprocessor ordering for owner updates.

findings.text: The validator offers contention and acquisition telemetry operations that receive a lock identity record together with a caller address and stay dormant unless both global statistics collection and validator enablement are active.

Diagnostic reporting operations expose interrupt history, held-lock enumeration, single-entry formatting with usage and wait-type details, symbolic name resolution with version and subclass decoration, and kernel release identification for inclusion in warning dumps.

Mutex debugging offers waiter lifecycle operations that prepare a fresh waiter with a self reference and empty queue linkage plus a poisoned exchange context, validate queue insertion against an existing blocker, enforce task agreement on removal while clearing linkage and ownership, and scrub a released waiter after asserting it is unlinked, with build variants that compile these hooks to inert placeholders.

Validator activity is permitted only while a global correctness flag remains set and neither the current processor reentry counter nor the current task reentry marker indicates nested validator execution.
Reentry suppression uses a per-processor counter that is raised on guarded entry and lowered on guarded exit, with an unbalanced exit producing a one-time diagnostic and a reset to the neutral value.

Saved processor flag state is cross-checked against tracked hard interrupt enablement and, outside hard interrupt service and outside fully preemptible real-time builds, against tracked soft interrupt enablement, with any divergence raising a correctness warning that suggests unannotated transitions and with a disabled validator triggering a dump of recent interrupt transitions.

Contention and acquisition accounting skip a distinguished untracked sentinel key and otherwise apply only when the current task shows nonzero held depth with a successful held-stack search whose located entry refers to the same lock identity before any timestamp or counter update occurs.

Per-class counters live in processor-local storage indexed by offset from the class table base, while call-site tables retain only a bounded number of distinct addresses per class with an overflow index indicating that no further distinct sites are recorded.

Held-stack lookup begins at the most recently acquired entry and moves toward older entries, terminating without success when it would cross entries recorded under different interrupt contexts and reporting both the located entry position and its index.

A held entry is considered to match a queried lock when the stored instance pointer is identical, or when the entry carries reference aliasing with a resolvable class and a companion nesting marker, in which case equality of the stored class index against the resolved class position also establishes a match, while an unresolvable class or missing nesting marker yields no match.

Class resolution derives a subclass key by offsetting from the lock key base, rejects out-of-range subclass requests by disabling validation with a diagnostic dump, returns absent when the lock key is uninitialized, requires interrupts to be disabled during hash traversal under read-side protection, and warns when an identical key is found under an unexpected name unless the lock opts out of validation.

A cached class pointer is trusted only alongside a present lock key with an in-range subclass selector, where the pointer itself is non-null and lies within the class table extent with a live slot and points back to the expected subclass key storage.
Interval accumulation preserves the largest and smallest observed durations along with a running total and a sample count, initializing the minimum from the first sample.

Mutex ownership is encoded as a single atomic word that fuses an owning task identity with a small flag set, where masking isolates either the task portion or the flag portion and where atomic bitwise updates set or clear individual flags without disturbing the task portion.

Ownership encodings observe stable constraints where an empty owner carries no transfer markers, a pickup request is satisfiable only by the recorded owner, and a handoff marker once set blocks competing handoff claims until ownership moves.

The wait queue maintains coherence where an empty queue shows a null first pointer with no waiters indication while a populated queue shows a non-null first pointer that denotes the earliest waiter and remains reachable through linkage.

Usage rendering derives two characters per abstract state from mask bits, where a dot marks the safest default, a plus marks enabled outside interrupt context, a minus marks presence inside with disabled state, and a query mark marks presence inside with enabled state, while companion tables for names and handlers arise from repeated expansion over a shared state catalogue with explicit sentinel entries for initial and non-maskable contexts.
Telemetry accounting preserves the local interrupt enablement across its guarded region, restoring the saved state on exit.
Wait queue insertion and removal each assume the caller already holds the dedicated queue spin protection across the update.

Observation of the task blocker field is serialized by the per-task blocker spin protection held for the duration of the read, while class hash traversal expects read-side protection with interrupts disabled.

Validator side records show identity maps with key and name alongside class_cache plus cpu and ip markers, held entries with instance and class_idx alongside references and nest_lock plus irq_context and waittime_stamp with holdtime_stamp and read plus acquire_ip, classes with key and name alongside name_version and subclass plus usage_mask and wait types with contention tables and print_fn, and tasks with lockdep_depth and held_locks alongside lockdep_recursion and softirqs_enabled plus irqtrace and comm with blocked_lock.

Statistics and synchronization records show per-class counters with contention_point and contending_point alongside bounces plus read_waittime and write_waittime, timing summaries with max and min alongside total and nr, mutexes with owner and wait_lock alongside first_waiter, and waiters with magic and list alongside ww_ctx and task.

Wait tracking distinguishes an idle condition, a waiting condition marked by a contention timestamp, and a held condition marked by a hold timestamp with accumulated wait duration and updated holder location, where cross-processor movement is counted separately.

Validation operates between an active mode and a terminal disabled mode entered on severe inconsistency, where reentry depth returns to neutral after each guarded region and any imbalance triggers a one-time diagnostic with reset, while disabled mode suppresses further telemetry and diagnostics.

Several inconsistencies raise diagnostics and may permanently disable validation, including accounting with empty depth, subclass requests beyond the supported range, class positions that fail liveness checks, queue teardown while still linked, insertion when a blocker is already recorded, and removal where the recorded waiter task or blocker identity disagrees.

Held-lock dumps for tasks that may run elsewhere are explicitly best effort and can observe concurrent mutation of entries, release and clearing underfoot, and stale processor or running-state indications, with unresolvable entries rendered as a released placeholder rather than dereferenced.

Symbolic limits govern capacities where LOCKSTAT_POINTS bounds per-class site tables alongside MAX_LOCKDEP_SUBCLASSES plus MAX_LOCKDEP_KEYS bounding class dimensions, while MUTEX_FLAGS isolates control bits alongside MUTEX_FLAG_WAITERS plus MUTEX_FLAG_HANDOFF plus MUTEX_FLAG_PICKUP marking queue and transfer states, with MUTEX_DEBUG_INIT plus MUTEX_DEBUG_FREE as waiter fill patterns and BLOCKER_TYPE_MUTEX tagging mutex blocking.

Telemetry entry points for contention and acquisition serve as the sole gated access to internal accounting, remaining inert without statistics and enablement and otherwise delegating to internal helpers under interrupt preservation and reentry suppression.
